claim: PLK-1 phosphorylates the single Caenorhabditis elegans lamin (LMN-1) to trigger lamina depolymerization during mitosis.
source: Previously, we reported that the Polo-like kinase PLK-1 phosphorylates the single Caenorhabditis elegans lamin (LMN-1) to trigger lamina depolymerization during mitosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Velez-Aguilera et al., 2020) mentioned in the abstract.

claim: PLK-1-mediated lamina depolymerization is required to form a pronuclear envelope scission event that removes membranes on the juxtaposed oocyte and sperm pronuclear envelopes in the zygote.
source: We showed that this event is required to form a pronuclear envelope scission event that removes membranes on the juxtaposed oocyte and sperm pronuclear envelopes in the zygote, allowing the parental chromosomes to merge in a single nucleus after segregation (Velez-Aguilera et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Velez-Aguilera et al., 2020).

claim: Cortical microtubule pulling forces contribute to pronuclear envelopes scission by promoting mitotic spindle elongation.
source: Here, we show that cortical microtubule pulling forces contribute to pronuclear envelopes scission by promoting mitotic spindle elongation, and conversely, nuclear envelopes remodeling facilitates spindle elongation.
evidence: This claim is presented as a finding of the current study in the abstract.

claim: Nuclear envelopes remodeling facilitates spindle elongation.
source: Here, we show that cortical microtubule pulling forces contribute to pronuclear envelopes scission by promoting mitotic spindle elongation, and conversely, nuclear envelopes remodeling facilitates spindle elongation.
evidence: This claim is presented as a finding of the current study in the abstract.

claim: Weakening the pronuclear envelopes via PLK-1-mediated lamina depolymerization is a prerequisite for the astral microtubule pulling forces to trigger pronuclear membranes scission.
source: We also demonstrate that weakening the pronuclear envelopes via PLK-1-mediated lamina depolymerization, is a prerequisite for the astral microtubule pulling forces to trigger pronuclear membranes scission.
evidence: This claim is presented as a finding of the current study in the abstract.

claim: PLK-1 mainly acts via lamina depolymerization in pronuclear envelopes scission.
source: Finally, we provide evidence that PLK-1 mainly acts via lamina depolymerization in this process.
evidence: This claim is presented as a finding of the current study in the abstract.

claim: Temporal coordination between lamina depolymerization and mitotic spindle elongation facilitates pronuclear envelopes scission and parental genomes unification.
source: These observations thus indicate that temporal coordination between lamina depolymerization and mitotic spindle elongation facilitates pronuclear envelopes scission and parental genomes unification.
evidence: This claim is presented as a conclusion in the abstract based on the study's findings.

claim: The Caenorhabditis elegans zygote provides an attractive model system to investigate the mechanisms by which the maternal and paternal genomes unify at the beginning of life.
source: The Caenorhabditis elegans zygote provides an attractive model system to investigate the mechanisms by which the maternal and paternal genomes unify at the beginning of life (Oegema and Hyman, 2006; Cohen-Fix and Askjaer, 2017; Pintard and Bowerman, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: After fertilization, the oocyte and sperm chromosomes surrounded by a nuclear envelope localize to opposite sides of the zygote.
source: After fertilization, the oocyte and sperm chromosomes surrounded by a nuclear envelope localize to opposite sides of the zygote.
evidence: This claim describes established knowledge about C. elegans zygote biology.

claim: The female pronucleus is located in the anterior, whereas the male pronucleus—and associated centrosomes—is in the posterior.
source: The female pronucleus is located in the anterior, whereas the male pronucleus—and associated centrosomes—is in the posterior.
evidence: This claim describes established knowledge about C. elegans zygote biology.

claim: When the two pronuclei meet, they change their shape, flattening out along their juxtaposed sides, eventually aligning along the AP axis of the one-cell embryo.
source: When the two pronuclei meet, they change their shape, flattening out along their juxtaposed sides, eventually aligning along the AP axis of the one-cell embryo (Oegema and Hyman, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: C. elegans encodes a single lamin (LMN-1), closer to vertebrate B-type than A-type lamins.
source: C. elegans encodes a single lamin (LMN-1), closer to vertebrate B-type than A-type lamins (Liu et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: In the C. elegans zygote, mitosis is semi-open, and the nuclear envelope only partially breaks down during spindle assembly.
source: In the C. elegans zygote, mitosis is semi-open, and the nuclear envelope only partially breaks down during spindle assembly (Cohen-Fix and Askjaer, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: NPC disassembly and lamina depolymerization starts in the vicinity of the centrosomes and then later on the juxtaposed envelopes located between the parental chromosomes.
source: NPC disassembly and lamina depolymerization starts in the vicinity of the centrosomes and then later on the juxtaposed envelopes located between the parental chromosomes (Lee et al., 2000; Hachet et al., 2012; Velez-Aguilera et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Complete removal of the NPCs and the lamina only occurs in early anaphase.
source: Complete removal of the NPCs and the lamina only occurs in early anaphase (Lee et al., 2000; Hachet et al., 2012; Velez-Aguilera et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Removal of the membranes between the parental chromosomes begins with the formation of a membrane scission event (also called a membrane gap), visible by fluorescent microscopy by labeling INM proteins (e.g., LEM-2).
source: Removal of the membranes between the parental chromosomes begins with the formation of a membrane scission event (also called a membrane gap), visible by fluorescent microscopy by labeling INM proteins (e.g., LEM-2) (Audhya et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The membrane scission event occurs concomitantly with the parental chromosomes congressing on the metaphase plate, 10–40 s before anaphase onset.
source: This event occurs concomitantly with the parental chromosomes congressing on the metaphase plate, 10–40 s before anaphase onset (Audhya et al., 2007; Rahman et al., 2020), allowing the chromosomes from the two pronuclei to mingle on the metaphase plate and join in a single nucleus after chromosome segregation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The membrane scission event always appears at an equal distance from the two centrosomes and depends on the proper alignment of the chromosomes on the metaphase plate.
source: Intriguingly, it always appears at an equal distance from the two centrosomes and depends on the proper alignment of the chromosomes on the metaphase plate (Rahman et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Membrane scission is totally prevented in hcp-3CENPA(RNAi) embryos that fail to assemble kinetochores and are defective in chromosome alignment.
source: Consistently, membrane scission is totally prevented in hcp-3CENPA(RNAi) embryos (Rahman et al., 2015) that fail to assemble kinetochores and are defective in chromosome alignment (Oegema et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Formation of the membrane gap requires depolymerization of the lamina by the mitotic Polo-like kinase PLK-1.
source: Formation of this membrane gap also requires depolymerization of the lamina by the mitotic Polo-like kinase PLK-1 (Rahman et al., 2015; Martino et al., 2017; Velez-Aguilera et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Expression of an LMN-1 version carrying eight non-phosphorylable alanines replacing serines (LMN-1 8A) is sufficient to prevent the formation of pronuclear envelopes scission.
source: Accordingly, expression of an LMN-1 version, carrying eight non-phosphorylable alanines replacing serines (hereafter LMN-1 8A), is sufficient to prevent the formation of pronuclear envelopes scission.
evidence: This claim describes an experimental observation from previous work.

claim: A failure to form membranes scission can result in the appearance of embryos with a paired nuclei phenotype.
source: A failure to form this membranes scission can result in the appearance of embryos with a paired nuclei phenotype (Rahman et al., 2015; Martino et al., 2017; Velez-Aguilera et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In paired nuclei embryos, the two sets of parental chromosomes remain physically separated during mitosis and segregate into two separate DNA masses at each pole of the spindle.
source: In these embryos, the two sets of parental chromosomes remain physically separated during mitosis and segregate into two separate DNA masses at each pole of the spindle.
evidence: This claim describes the paired nuclei phenotype based on previous observations.

claim: Pronuclear envelopes permeabilization was detected around 160 s before anaphase onset, concomitantly with pronuclear membranes deformation near the centrosomes.
source: Pronuclear envelopes permeabilization, measured by the appearance of soluble tubulin in the pronuclei space, was detected around 160 s before anaphase onset, concomitantly with pronuclear membranes deformation near the centrosomes (Figure 1A–D, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1A-D and associated source data.

claim: Nuclear envelope permeabilization was systematically detected first in the male pronucleus.
source: Nuclear envelope permeabilization was systematically detected first in the male pronucleus (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Signs of lamina disappearance from the pronuclear envelopes systematically started in the vicinity of centrosomes, 70 s before anaphase onset.
source: Signs of lamina disappearance from the pronuclear envelopes systematically started in the vicinity of centrosomes, 70 s before anaphase onset (Figure 1A and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2), possibly as a consequence of microtubule pulling at this site, together with the action of the lamin kinase PLK-1, which is enriched at centrosomes (Chase et al., 2000; Budirahardja and Gönczy, 2008; Nishi et al., 2008; Martino et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1A and D, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2, along with citations to previous literature.

claim: Lamina disassembly between the pronuclei started only 50 s before anaphase onset.
source: Lamina disassembly between the pronuclei started only 50 s before anaphase onset (Figure 1A and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1A and D.

claim: The membrane scission event between the juxtaposed pronuclei was detected around 30 s before anaphase onset.
source: The membrane scission event between the juxtaposed pronuclei was detected later, around 30 s before anaphase onset (Figure 1B and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), consistent with previous observations (Audhya et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1B and D, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and citation to previous literature.

claim: The membrane scission event appeared immediately after chromosome alignment on the metaphase plate.
source: The membrane scission event appeared immediately after chromosome alignment on the metaphase plate (Figure 1B, red arrowhead, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: Starting 80 s before anaphase onset, the distance between the centrosomes steadily increased as a result of spindle elongation.
source: Starting 80 s before anaphase onset, the distance between the centrosomes steadily increased as a result of spindle elongation (Figure 1F, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1F and Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: The beginning of spindle elongation was concomitant with lamina depolymerization but preceded membrane gap formation.
source: The beginning of spindle elongation was concomitant with lamina depolymerization but preceded membrane gap formation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the timing data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Mild depletion of GPR-1/2 in gfp::lmn-1 8A embryos greatly enhanced the percentage of embryos presenting a paired nuclei phenotype, with nearly 54% showing double-paired nuclei and 24% a single-paired nuclei.
source: Mild depletion of GPR-1/2 in gfp::lmn-1 8A embryos greatly enhanced the percentage of embryos presenting a paired nuclei phenotype, with nearly 54% showing double-paired nuclei and 24% a single-paired nuclei (Figure 2A, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: More severe RNAi-mediated gpr-1/2 inactivation further increased the percentage of gfp::lmn-1 8A mutant embryos presenting a double-paired nuclei phenotype to 83%.
source: More severe RNAi-mediated gpr-1/2 inactivation (Materials and methods) further increased the percentage of gfp::lmn-1 8A mutant embryos presenting a double-paired nuclei phenotype to 83% (Figure 2A, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Similar treatments of the embryos expressing a wild-type (WT) GFP::LMN-1 allele had only little effect with 5% of embryos presenting a double-paired nuclei phenotype and 4% presenting a single-paired nuclei phenotype.
source: Similar treatments of the embryos expressing a wild-type (WT) GFP::LMN-1 allele had only little effect with 5% of embryos presenting a double-paired nuclei phenotype and 4% presenting a single-paired nuclei phenotype (Figure 2A, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Reduction of cortical microtubule pulling forces enhances the paired nuclei phenotype of embryos with a partially stabilized lamina network.
source: Thus, reduction of cortical microtubule pulling forces enhances the paired nuclei phenotype of embryos with a partially stabilized lamina network.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on gpr-1/2 RNAi effects.

claim: Microtubule pulling forces facilitate the union of the parental chromosomes in the one-cell embryo.
source: These observations indicate that microtubule pulling forces facilitate the union of the parental chromosomes in the one-cell embryo.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on gpr-1/2 RNAi effects.

claim: gpr-1/2 inactivation had no discernable effect on GFP::LMN-1 WT disassembly.
source: gpr-1/2 inactivation had no discernable effect on GFP::LMN-1 WT disassembly (Figure 2C and E, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2C and E, and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Partial gpr-1/2 inactivation did not significantly stabilize GFP::LMN-1 8A during mitosis.
source: Likewise, partial gpr-1/2 inactivation did not significantly stabilize GFP::LMN-1 8A during mitosis (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and associated source data.

claim: More severe reduction of cortical microtubule pulling forces, using strong RNAi-mediated gpr-1/2 inactivation, did stabilize GFP::LMN-1 8A.
source: However, more severe reduction of cortical microtubule pulling forces, using strong RNAi-mediated gpr-1/2 inactivation, did stabilize GFP::LMN-1 8A (Figure 2D and F, Figure 2—source data 1), indicating that microtubule pulling forces contribute to lamina disassembly during mitosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2D and F, and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Microtubule pulling forces contribute to lamina disassembly during mitosis.
source: However, more severe reduction of cortical microtubule pulling forces, using strong RNAi-mediated gpr-1/2 inactivation, did stabilize GFP::LMN-1 8A (Figure 2D and F, Figure 2—source data 1), indicating that microtubule pulling forces contribute to lamina disassembly during mitosis.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on gpr-1/2 RNAi effects on GFP::LMN-1 8A.

claim: Loss of klp-7 caused a premature disassembly of GFP::LMN-1 8A during mitosis.
source: Loss of klp-7 caused a premature disassembly of GFP::LMN-1 8A during mitosis (Figure 2D and F, Figure 2—source data 1), again arguing that astral microtubule pulling forces contribute to the union of the parental chromosomes, at least in part by pulling at the lamina during mitosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2D and F, and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Astral microtubule pulling forces contribute to the union of the parental chromosomes, at least in part by pulling at the lamina during mitosis.
source: Loss of klp-7 caused a premature disassembly of GFP::LMN-1 8A during mitosis (Figure 2D and F, Figure 2—source data 1), again arguing that astral microtubule pulling forces contribute to the union of the parental chromosomes, at least in part by pulling at the lamina during mitosis.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on klp-7 RNAi effects.

claim: In control embryos, the membrane scission event between the pronuclei was systematically observed around 30 s before anaphase onset, after chromosomes alignment on the metaphase plate (n=32).
source: In control embryos, the membrane scission event between the pronuclei was systematically observed around 30 s before anaphase onset, after chromosomes alignment on the metaphase plate (n=32) (Figure 3B, red arrowhead).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 3B.

claim: In a vast majority of gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos, the membrane scission between the pronuclei was never detected.
source: However, in a vast majority of gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos, the membrane scission between the pronuclei was never detected.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations on gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos.

claim: Of the 30 gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos analyzed, only 4 presented a membrane scission event (13%).
source: Of the 30 embryos analyzed, only 4 presented a membrane scission event (13%) (Figure 3B and C, Figure 3—source data 1) and these 4 embryos were also the least affected in spindle elongation (Figure 3D, Figure 3—source data 1), suggesting that spindle elongation contributes to pronuclei membrane scission.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 3B, C, and D, and Figure 3—source data 1.

claim: Spindle elongation contributes to pronuclei membrane scission.
source: Of the 30 embryos analyzed, only 4 presented a membrane scission event (13%) (Figure 3B and C, Figure 3—source data 1) and these 4 embryos were also the least affected in spindle elongation (Figure 3D, Figure 3—source data 1), suggesting that spindle elongation contributes to pronuclei membrane scission.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the correlation between spindle elongation and membrane scission in gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos.

claim: All reforming nuclei were severely misshapen in gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos, but only a fraction of them presented a double-paired nuclei phenotype at the two-cell stage.
source: Notably, all reforming nuclei were severely misshapen in gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos, but only a fraction of them presented a double-paired nuclei phenotype at the two-cell stage (Figure 3E, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 3E and Figure 3—source data 1.

claim: In 50% of efa-6 and klp-7(RNAi) embryos, pronuclear membranes scission occurred between 40 and 120 s before anaphase onset.
source: While the control embryos underwent membrane scission between the juxtaposed pronuclei 0–30 s before anaphase onset, this event occurred systematically earlier in efa-6 and klp-7(RNAi) embryos. In 50% of these embryos, pronuclear membranes scission occurred between 40 and 120 s before anaphase onset (Figure 4B and C, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 4B and C, and Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: Membrane scission occurred earlier in efa-6 and klp-7(RNAi) embryos as a consequence of premature mitotic spindle elongation.
source: Membrane scission occurred earlier in these embryos as a consequence of premature mitotic spindle elongation (Figure 4D, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 4D and Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: Membranes scission systematically occurred at a similar mitotic spindle length.
source: By measuring mitotic spindle length at the time of membrane gap formation, we noticed that membranes scission systematically occurred at a similar mitotic spindle length (Figure 4E, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 4E and Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: Microtubule pulling forces, by promoting mitotic spindle elongation, contribute to pronuclear membranes scission, possibly by tearing apart the pronuclear membranes.
source: Taken together, these observations indicate that microtubule pulling forces, by promoting mitotic spindle elongation, contribute to pronuclear membranes scission, possibly by tearing apart the pronuclear membranes.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on efa-6 and klp-7 RNAi effects.

claim: In contrast to WT, the spindle did not elongate to the same extent in lmn-1 8A mutant embryos.
source: In contrast to WT, the spindle did not elongate to the same extent in lmn-1 8A mutant embryos (Figure 5A, Figure 5—source data 1), indicating that stabilization of the lamina interferes with mitotic spindle elongation and thus that lamina depolymerization facilitates spindle elongation.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5A and Figure 5—source data 1.

claim: Stabilization of the lamina interferes with mitotic spindle elongation.
source: In contrast to WT, the spindle did not elongate to the same extent in lmn-1 8A mutant embryos (Figure 5A, Figure 5—source data 1), indicating that stabilization of the lamina interferes with mitotic spindle elongation and thus that lamina depolymerization facilitates spindle elongation.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on lmn-1 8A mutant embryos.

claim: Lamina depolymerization facilitates spindle elongation.
source: In contrast to WT, the spindle did not elongate to the same extent in lmn-1 8A mutant embryos (Figure 5A, Figure 5—source data 1), indicating that stabilization of the lamina interferes with mitotic spindle elongation and thus that lamina depolymerization facilitates spindle elongation.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on lmn-1 8A mutant embryos.

claim: klp-7 inactivation in lmn-1 8A embryos rescued mitotic spindle elongation defects.
source: While these treatments rescued mitotic spindle elongation defects of lmn-1 8A embryos (Figure 5B, Figure 5—source data 1), they failed to restore the formation of pronuclear membranes scission and single nucleus embryos at the two-cell stage (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5B and Figure 5—source data 1.

claim: klp-7 inactivation in lmn-1 8A embryos failed to restore the formation of pronuclear membranes scission and single nucleus embryos at the two-cell stage.
source: While these treatments rescued mitotic spindle elongation defects of lmn-1 8A embryos (Figure 5B, Figure 5—source data 1), they failed to restore the formation of pronuclear membranes scission and single nucleus embryos at the two-cell stage (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Even premature and excessive spindle elongation is not sufficient to induce membrane scission when the lamina is stabilized during mitosis.
source: These observations indicate that even premature and excessive spindle elongation is not sufficient to induce membrane scission when the lamina is stabilized during mitosis.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on klp-7 RNAi in lmn-1 8A embryos.

claim: Lamina depolymerization is a prerequisite for pronuclear envelopes scission.
source: Collectively, these observations indicate that lamina depolymerization is a prerequisite for pronuclear envelopes scission.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on lmn-1 8A embryos.

claim: In efa-6 or klp-7(RNAi) embryos with enhanced astral pulling forces, pronuclear membranes scission often occurred before chromosomes were fully aligned on the metaphase plate.
source: In the efa-6 or klp-7(RNAi) embryos with enhanced astral pulling forces, pronuclear membranes scission often occurred before chromosomes were fully aligned on the metaphase plate (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) suggesting that membrane scission between the pronuclei may not require full and complete chromosome alignment on the metaphase plate.
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Membrane scission between the pronuclei may not require full and complete chromosome alignment on the metaphase plate.
source: In the efa-6 or klp-7(RNAi) embryos with enhanced astral pulling forces, pronuclear membranes scission often occurred before chromosomes were fully aligned on the metaphase plate (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) suggesting that membrane scission between the pronuclei may not require full and complete chromosome alignment on the metaphase plate.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that membrane scission can occur before full chromosome alignment in efa-6 or klp-7(RNAi) embryos.

claim: In klp-7 and hcp-3 double inactivation embryos, no membrane scission was detected despite the extensive mitotic spindle elongation.
source: In these embryos, no membrane scission was detected despite the extensive mitotic spindle elongation (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 5C.

claim: Chromosome localization in the vicinity of the pronuclear membranes is necessary for pronuclear membranes scission and might dictate the site of membranes scission.
source: These observations indicate that chromosome localization in the vicinity of the pronuclear membranes is necessary for pronuclear membranes scission and might dictate the site of membranes scission.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on klp-7 and hcp-3 double inactivation embryos.

claim: PLK-1 is critically required for pronuclear envelopes scission.
source: PLK-1 is critically required for pronuclear envelopes scission (Rahman et al., 2015; Martino et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Membranes scission is prevented in plk-1ts embryos.
source: Accordingly, membranes scission is prevented in plk-1ts embryos.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about plk-1ts embryos.

claim: LMN-1 is a key PLK-1 target in pronuclear envelopes scission as the sole expression of the non-phosphorylable lmn-1 8A allele is sufficient to prevent pronuclear envelopes scission.
source: We previously showed that LMN-1 is a key PLK-1 target in this process as the sole expression of the non-phosphorylable lmn-1 8A allele is sufficient to prevent pronuclear envelopes scission (Velez-Aguilera et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Partial RNAi-mediated lmn-1 inactivation was sufficient to restore pronuclear envelopes scission in plk-1ts embryos.
source: However, partial RNAi-mediated lmn-1 inactivation was sufficient to restore pronuclear envelopes scission (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 6B.

claim: lmn-1 inactivation suppressed the paired nuclei phenotype of plk-1ts embryos.
source: lmn-1 inactivation also suppressed the paired nuclei phenotype of plk-1ts embryos in these conditions (Figure 6C, Figure 6—source data 1), as reported previously (Rahman et al., 2015; Martino et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 6C and Figure 6—source data 1, and citations to previous literature.

claim: lmn-1 inactivation not only restored membrane scission and the shape of the pronuclei, but also the normal localization of LEM-2 and EMR-1.
source: lmn-1 inactivation not only restored membrane scission and the shape of the pronuclei, but also the normal localization of LEM-2 and EMR-1.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the experiments on plk-1ts embryos with lmn-1 inactivation.

claim: LMN-1 might be the only PLK-1 direct target involved in regulating pronuclear membranes scission.
source: Collectively, these observations suggest that LMN-1 might be the only PLK-1 direct target involved in regulating pronuclear membranes scission.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on plk-1ts embryos with lmn-1 inactivation.

claim: Cortical microtubule pulling forces are required for pronuclear membranes scission but are not sufficient when chromosomes are not aligned on the metaphase plate, or when the lamina persists between the parental chromosomes.
source: In conclusion, our study indicates that cortical microtubule pulling forces are required for pronuclear membranes scission but are not sufficient when chromosomes are not aligned on the metaphase plate, or when the lamina persists between the parental chromosomes.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the overall findings of the study.

claim: Coordination between chromosome alignment, lamina depolymerization, and mitotic spindle elongation is required for pronuclear envelopes scission in the early C. elegans embryo.
source: Coordination between chromosome alignment, lamina depolymerization, and mitotic spindle elongation is thus required for pronuclear envelopes scission in the early C. elegans embryo (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the overall findings of the study and is illustrated in Figure 6D.

claim: A lack of membrane scission does not systematically result in a paired nuclei phenotype.
source: In addition, our results indicate that a lack of membrane scission does not systematically result in a paired nuclei phenotype.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations on gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos.

claim: While gpr-1/2 inactivation prevents membrane scission, most reforming nuclei were misshapen but not double paired at the two-cell stage.
source: While gpr-1/2 inactivation prevents membrane scission, most reforming nuclei were misshapen but not double paired at the two-cell stage.
evidence: This claim is based on observations from the experiments on gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos.

claim: In all reported conditions where a correlation between a lack of membrane scission and the paired nuclei phenotype was observed, depolymerization of the lamina was systematically delayed or inhibited.
source: It is noteworthy that in all reported conditions where a correlation between a lack of membrane scission and the paired nuclei phenotype was observed, depolymerization of the lamina was systematically delayed or inhibited (Audhya et al., 2007; Galy et al., 2008; Golden et al., 2009; Bahmanyar et al., 2014; Rahman et al., 2015; Martino et al., 2017; Velez-Aguilera et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Persistence of the lamina rigidifies the nuclear membrane, prevents the redistribution of integral membrane proteins into the ER, and counteracts the mitotic spindle elongation, which typically results in a penetrant paired nuclei phenotype.
source: Persistence of the lamina rigidifies the nuclear membrane, prevents the redistribution of integral membrane proteins into the ER, and counteracts the mitotic spindle elongation, which typically results in a penetrant paired nuclei phenotype.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the overall findings and previous literature.

claim: A defective lamina depolymerization interferes with mitotic spindle elongation, highlighting the role of nuclear envelope remodeling in influencing mitotic spindle length.
source: Finally, our observations that a defective lamina depolymerization interferes with mitotic spindle elongation highlights the role of nuclear envelope remodeling in influencing mitotic spindle length.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations on lmn-1 8A mutant embryos.

claim: Before NEBD, 200 s prior to anaphase onset, microtubules were excluded from the pronuclei space.
source: Before NEBD, 200 s prior to anaphase onset, microtubules were excluded from the pronuclei space, and the pronuclear envelopes appeared flattened along their juxtaposed sides but presented elsewhere a rounded shape, except around centrosomes where the nuclear envelopes were highly curved (90° angle) (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1A and B.

claim: The pronuclear envelopes appeared flattened along their juxtaposed sides but presented elsewhere a rounded shape, except around centrosomes where the nuclear envelopes were highly curved (90° angle).
source: Before NEBD, 200 s prior to anaphase onset, microtubules were excluded from the pronuclei space, and the pronuclear envelopes appeared flattened along their juxtaposed sides but presented elsewhere a rounded shape, except around centrosomes where the nuclear envelopes were highly curved (90° angle) (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1A and B.

claim: 160 s before anaphase onset, signs of nuclear envelope deformation were apparent in the vicinity of the centrosomes.
source: Later, 160 s before anaphase onset, signs of nuclear envelope deformation were apparent in the vicinity of the centrosomes (Figure 1A, red arrow).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1A.

claim: At sites near centrosomes, the pronuclear envelopes appeared deformed toward the centrosomes, with the appearance of protrusions, suggesting that microtubules, emanating from the centrosomes were pulling on the pronuclear envelopes.
source: At these sites, the pronuclear envelopes appeared deformed toward the centrosomes, with the appearance of protrusions, suggesting that microtubules, emanating from the centrosomes were pulling on the pronuclear envelopes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation of pronuclear envelope deformation near centrosomes.

claim: As more microtubules invaded the pronuclei space to capture paternal chromosomes, the overall surface of the pronuclei decreased.
source: As more microtubules invaded the pronuclei space to capture paternal chromosomes, the overall surface of the pronuclei decreased (Figure 1E, Figure 1—source data 1), and the pronuclei adopted a more triangular shape, possibly dictated by microtubules assembling the mitotic spindle in the space confined by the remnants of the pronuclear envelopes (Figure 1B; Hayashi et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1E and Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: The pronuclei adopted a more triangular shape, possibly dictated by microtubules assembling the mitotic spindle in the space confined by the remnants of the pronuclear envelopes.
source: As more microtubules invaded the pronuclei space to capture paternal chromosomes, the overall surface of the pronuclei decreased (Figure 1E, Figure 1—source data 1), and the pronuclei adopted a more triangular shape, possibly dictated by microtubules assembling the mitotic spindle in the space confined by the remnants of the pronuclear envelopes (Figure 1B; Hayashi et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is inferred from observations and supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The lamina progressively disappeared in the vicinity of the centrosomes but persisted between the parental chromosomes.
source: The lamina progressively disappeared in the vicinity of the centrosomes but persisted between the parental chromosomes.
evidence: This claim is based on observations of lamina dynamics during NEBD.

claim: At 50 s before anaphase onset, the lamina network was still detected on the nuclear envelope remnants surrounding the chromosomes.
source: At this time point, the lamina network was still detected on the nuclear envelope remnants surrounding the chromosomes (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1A.

claim: By pulling on nuclear envelopes and membranes, and by tearing apart the lamina and by elongating the mitotic spindle, astral microtubule pulling forces might contribute to pronuclear envelopes breakdown.
source: Based on these observations, we hypothesized that by pulling on nuclear envelopes and membranes, and by tearing apart the lamina and by elongating the mitotic spindle, astral microtubule pulling forces might contribute to pronuclear envelopes breakdown, and thus to the unification of the parental chromosomes in the early C. elegans embryo.
evidence: This claim is a hypothesis based on the observations of microtubule dynamics and lamina disassembly.

claim: The paired nuclei phenotype is a visual readout of the failure to properly remove the nuclear envelope between the pronuclei.
source: The paired nuclei phenotype is a visual readout of the failure to properly remove the nuclear envelope between the pronuclei (Audhya et al., 2007; Bahmanyar et al., 2014; Galy et al., 2008; Rahman et al., 2015; Martino et al., 2017; Velez-Aguilera et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: 8% of the embryos expressing GFP::LMN-1 8A present double-paired nuclei at the two-cell stage, and another 9% present a single-paired nuclei cell.
source: Because this allele partially stabilizes the lamina, 8% of the embryos expressing GFP::LMN-1 8A present double-paired nuclei at the two-cell stage, and another 9% present a single-paired nuclei cell (Figure 2A, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 2A and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: By fluidifying the pronuclear membranes, lamina depolymerization might facilitate the release of INM proteins back into the peripheral ER surrounding the centrosomes.
source: We speculate that by fluidifying the pronuclear membranes, lamina depolymerization might facilitate the release of INM proteins back into the peripheral ER surrounding the centrosomes.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning based on the observations of LEM-2 and EMR-1 localization.

claim: In gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos, the lamina disassembles, which results in membrane flexibility, and allows integral membrane proteins to redistribute into the peripheral ER.
source: One possible explanation for this observation is that the lamina disassembles in gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos, which results in membrane flexibility, and allows integral membrane proteins to redistribute into the peripheral ER.
evidence: This claim is speculative reasoning to explain why gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos don't always show paired nuclei despite lack of membrane scission.

claim: During nuclear envelopes reformation and expansion, the membrane separating the parental chromosomes is weak and eventually dismantles, which may explain why single pronuclei manage to form at the two-cell stage in gpr-1/2(RNAi) embryos.
